newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Misys aquisition spree not over.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Misys aquisition spree not over.

text.p: Misys Plc, Britain's fast-growing software supplier, said on Wednesday its acquisition spree was not yet over despite spending 67 million pounds on seven purchases last year.

"We are a fairly active business in terms of acquisitions," Misys' chairman Kevin Lomax told Reuters in an interview. "I wouldn't want to comment on particular things but there are always a handful of things in consultation."
After reporting record annual pre-tax profits of 62.5 million pounds, a rise of 24 percent over last year, Lomax said the group also expected overall growth at least in the high teens this year.

Misys supplies secure software packages to banks and insurers and has become one of the world's largest software companies after buying trading firms across the world amid increasing consolidation in the sector.

Orders were up 20 percent year-on-year despite the strength of sterling, the group said, adding that it was well-placed to take advantage of opportunities of new product demands in time for year 2000 as well as European monetary union.
The group blamed a five percent fall in profits at its insurance arm on investments in new areas. But it expects these to pay off this year with growth resuming.

"Banking is still growing very strongly," Lomax said. "We expect a resumption of growth in insurance...and therefore the full business is growing very well. The company's UK business has been showing growth more like 10 percent -- but overall we see growth traditionally in the high teens and we usually do a bit better than that."

Lomax says the company's main banking division deals with around 95 percent of the world's top 200 banks and provides 70 percent of group profits and 65 percent of revenues. The division saw organic growth of 15 percent in sales and 26 percent in profits last year.
Around half of group revenues of 325.5 million pounds now come from outside Britain.

But Misys, which finished the year with net bank borrowings of 11.2 million pounds, said it was not currently considering a listing on America's Nasdaq exchange although Lomax said the group might consider the possibility in the future.
The group has seen its profits surge from a mere 9.2 million pounds in 1992. It's shares have leapt almost in tandem and now value the group at around 1.2 billion pounds.
Despite some concerns that the stock might be top-heavy -- at around 20 times prospective earnings -- it jumped 20p to 14.30 pounds by mid-morning.
Loam said that compared to U.S. rivals of a similar size the shares were still trading at a discount. "I don't think our rating in comparison with our peers is a particular exception," he said.
Misys raised its total dividend 15 percent to 12.26p.
